history.p: The present cantata is one of the very few surviving works from Scheibe’s time in Hamburg. The manuscript is dated 27 October 1737. According to Scheibe, he was asked by Georg Philipp Telemann, who was leaving for Paris in late September, to take on some of his assignments and compose the remaining cantatas of the church year to the texts of Gottfried Behrndt, that is cantatas for the nineteenth to the twenty-fifth Sundays post Trinitatis. However, Scheibe only composed the present work for Telemann which was performed on 27 October, for the other cantatas are in style clearly by Telemann as well as in his hand. Scheibe has included a stringed instrument belonging to the lute family, colascione, which does not appear in any other of his works. The instrument was, however, very popular with Telemann who included it in more than 400 works. Scheibe’s cantata was copied by Johann Balthasar König in Frankfurt where it is still located; the original limp folder was later used for one of Telemann’s other works, ‘Ich will den Herrn loben’ and is now in Berlin.

annot.p: Scheibe mentions having composed several cantatas for Telemann while he was in Paris (19th–25th Sunday after Trinity).

incipText.p: So ofte Jesus großer Nahme bald Sünden tilgt, bald Zeichen thut
Zweifeln und Tadeln, verdrehen und schmähen
Du thörichte Vernunft, die sich durch falsches Wissen blehet
Gehe hin, und sprich zu diesem Volcke
Mit Blindheit ist die Welt geschlagen
Ach Gott ich hab nach solcher Arth, gar lang mit großen Schaden
Ach ja, der Sünden lust, die stets das gute von sich stößet, die treibt noch immerfort zu alten lügen
Ihr Hertze rennt im Heuchel-Schein zur Höllen-Pful hienein
Wach auf! ô Mensch vom Sünden-Schlaf, ermuntre dich verlohrnes Schaaf
